chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from some of our companions, from Ibn Faddal, from Marwan, from 'Abd al-Malik, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who bought something from the covering of the Ka'bah, then fulfilled some need with part of it, and some of it remained in his possession: is its sale permissible?
He عليه السلام said: "He may sell what he wishes, give away what he does not wish, benefit from it, and seek its barakah."
I said: "May the deceased be shrouded with it?" He عليه السلام said: "No."

key_terms.بَيْعُهُ: its sale; the legal sale of the item in question
key_terms.يَسْتَنْفِعُ بِهِ: he benefits from it or makes use of it
key_terms.يُكَفِّنُ: he shrouds the deceased with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell, gift, or use a piece of the Ka'bah's covering, and can a dead person be shrouded in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding an item taken from the covering of the Ka'bah after lawful purchase. It permits selling, gifting, and benefiting from it, while also acknowledging its barakah, but it forbids using it as a shroud for the deceased.
